verdicts.reason: Both lose the original's structure in the same way. The three flavour names are stacked in reverse order with their descriptors in a separate list that no longer matches them (Honey Rosemary ends up beside 'Bright & zesty'), two cans shrink to tiny stubs beside the CTA, and the supporting line is cramped between headline and list. A's hero can is small and its label can't be read; B's right-hand can is larger with a readable label, so B is a little less bad.

The two are essentially the same broken layout. A puts a small can at the far left and B puts it at the far right, but in both the names and descriptors are split and mismatched, two cans become tiny CTA-side stubs with clipped tops, and the can labels and fine print can't be read. Neither arrangement balances the banner better.

Both have the same reversed, mismatched flavour list and detached descriptors, plus the two shrunken can stubs beside the CTA. A at least keeps one can at a meaningful size with a legible SOLSTICE band, which preserves the key imagery. B's left can is tiny with an illegible label, so the product nearly disappears.

Both repeat the mismatched name and descriptor stacks and the tiny can stubs beside the CTA. B's larger logo, headline and can read better at banner size, but its logo and CTA crowd the top and bottom edges and the stubs nearly touch the bottom. A has calmer margins but smaller type and a smaller centred block, leaving a large dead area at the left.
